subject: ancient-greek
summary: Question text is clean and readable and the Greek in the attached passage renders properly with all accents. The main faults are in what is and is not attached: one card asks the student to scan 'the first line in the passage above' with no passage anywhere on the card, and the 'photographs' attachment for 2023 Q4(viii) opens on a page listing seven other Q4 questions instead of a photograph. Schemes are plain text and legible, but long ones are either a single semicolon-joined block or 16 loose tick boxes with the headings (messenger / Iokaste / Chorus / Kreon) buried inside the rows, and marks are rarely shown per point. Several cards carry a paper-level instruction ('Answer any three...', '[60]') above the question that means nothing on a single card. Phone and desktop render the same content without overflow.

issues.title: Question refers to a passage that is not on the card
issues.detail: Card 1 says 'Scan the first line in the passage above. Mark the quantities and name the metre.' No Greek passage or line is shown or attached, so the question cannot be answered from the card. The scheme answer is a scansion pattern for a line the student never sees.
issues.suggested_fix: Attach the prescribed passage (or print the first line in Greek above the question) and remove the word 'above' problem by showing it inline.

issues.title: Photograph attachment opens on a page of other questions
issues.detail: Card 6 (2023 Q4(viii)) button says 'The photographs printed with this question', but page 1 of 3 is the Q4 question page showing Q4(i) to (vii) in full (Pylos, Alexander, Thucydides, Sophocles etc.) before the student reaches any photograph.
issues.suggested_fix: Attach only the plate pages (A, B, C), or crop page 9 to the (viii) block; start the reader on the first photograph.

issues.title: Scansion scheme shown as a run of dashes and pipes
issues.detail: Card 1 scheme reads '– – u – | u – u – | – – u – Iambic Trimeter' in body text, repeated again in the grey footer strip. Without the Greek line underneath, the longs and shorts are not tied to any syllables.
issues.suggested_fix: Show a crop of the official scheme with the marks above the Greek line, or set the Greek line with the quantities above it in a monospaced block and 'Iambic Trimeter' on its own line.

issues.title: Long schemes lose their grouping
issues.detail: Card 5 shows 16 separate tick boxes for a 'two of four' short-note question; the four headings are fused into the first row of each group ('Kreon; Brother of Iokaste.', 'Chorus: Male elders of Thebes.') and nothing says only two groups are needed or what each point is worth. Card 7 does the opposite: one tick box holding eleven semicolon-joined facts about Aeschylus.
issues.suggested_fix: Group points under bold sub-headings per option (messenger, Iokaste, Chorus, Kreon) with a line 'any two, 5 marks each'; break card 7's block into a bulleted list.

issues.title: Confusing mark arithmetic and missing marks
issues.detail: Card 4 footnote says 'The examiner marks the first correct answers higher than the rest ((8 + 7) + (8 + 7))' with doubled brackets and no explanation that it is two notes at 15 each. Cards 2, 5, 6 and 7 show no marks on any point.
issues.suggested_fix: Write it as 'Two notes, 15 marks each (8 + 7)'. Show per-part marks where the scheme gives them.

issues.title: Paper-level instructions left above the question
issues.detail: 'Answer any three of the following questions. They carry ten marks each:-' and 'Answer any two of the following questions. (Each question carries thirty marks):- [60]' sit above a single question, including a stray '[60]' and ':-'. Card 8 says 'photographs A, B and C below' while only A is attached. Card 3's attached page also shows the alternative Section A translation task above the passage.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop the choice rubric from single-question cards or reword it ('One of the optional 10-mark questions'); crop the 2014 page to Section B.

issues.title: Topic label does not match the question
issues.detail: Cards 1 and 2 (Medea, metre) and card 5 (Oedipus) are filed under 'Prescribed Prose Text (e.g. Plato)' and 'Prescribed Homer' in the manifest although they are drama questions. Not visible on the card itself but affects filtering.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-tag to the prescribed drama topic.

good_examples.why: Short clear question, single clean photograph of the vase, two-line scheme that answers it directly.
Greek passage attached and rendered crisply; one-line scheme matches the question.
Four options each get one tidy scheme row with the heading in front.
